Try it out

Install Q2 Nova using the Q2’s built-in updater. It's easy to return to stock or switch to another firmware.

Q2 Nova v0.136

SHA-256: Pending release

From stock firmware

Install from
microSD.

  1. Mount the microSD card

    Mount your Q2's microSD over USB or directly with a card reader.

  2. Copy update.tar to the card

    Download the update.tar package and place it at the top level of the card, alongside its folders. Safely eject the card.

  3. Start the update

    On the stock player, open System settings → System Update → TF card update and confirm. Leave the card inserted and the player powered on until the Q2 restarts.

First setup

Use the wheel to enter URLs and credentials. For long addresses and passwords, you can also edit the settings on a computer.

  1. Join Wi-Fi

    Open Settings → Connections → Wi-Fi. Turn Wi-Fi on, choose Scan, then select your network. Enter its password if prompted. Once connected, Connected To shows your network name and IP address.

    Using Tailscale?

    Open Settings → Connections → Tailscale, turn it on and choose Sign In. Use the link to continue sign in on your phone or computer. Approve the device in Tailscale's Admin Console if necessary.

    You can now connect to your server by IP address or full tailnet name. MagicDNS is not currently supported.

  2. Connect to Navidrome

    Choose Set Up Server on the home screen. Enter the URL you use to open Navidrome under Address, then fill in User and Password. Choose Test Connection. Once it says Connected, open Music → Albums and select a track to play.

    To change these details later, open Settings → Connections → Navidrome Server.

  3. Add books and podcasts (optional)

    Open Settings → Connections → Audiobookshelf. Enter your server’s Address. In Audiobookshelf, generate an API key for your account and enter it on the Q2 under API Token. Choose Test Connection. When it shows Connected, select Sync Now to load your library.

Edit the settings on a computer

With the Q2 powered off, put its microSD card in a reader. Open Q2Mainline/config.toml in a text editor. The player creates this file on first startup with a writable card. Update the existing entries with your own details.

Example config file

If the Wi-Fi section contains networks = [], replace that line with the [[wifi.networks]] block below.

[wifi]
enabled = true

[[wifi.networks]]
ssid = "Your Wi-Fi name"
psk = "Your Wi-Fi password"

[server]
url = "https://music.example.com"
user = "Your Navidrome username"
password = "Your Navidrome password"

# Optional, for books and podcasts
[audiobookshelf]
url = "https://books.example.com"
token = "Your Audiobookshelf API key"

Save the file, safely eject the card and put it back in the Q2 before powering on. Use Test Connection in the server’s settings to check the result.

Source code

The five upstream forks are public. Q2-specific changes are being prepared for release.

q2-player
The music player, desktop and browser simulators, and the release recipe for the complete update.tar.
q2-os
The Q2 operating system, including system services, the SDK, installer and recovery tools.
q2-toolchain
Builds the C and Rust cross-compilers for the X2000 from matching LLVM and Rust revisions.
q2-factory
Planned home for coding-agent workflows, test media, and end-to-end tests on the emulator and real player.
linux
Linux kernel fork for the Q2 board, device drivers and kernel configuration.
buildroot
Buildroot fork for changes to the build system used by q2-os.
llvm-project
LLVM and Clang fork for X2000 code generation and compiler target support.
rust
Rust compiler and standard library sources used by q2-toolchain.
qemu
QEMU fork for the XBurst CPU, X2000 peripherals and Q2 device model.
